Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and a few items we need to confirm so we can scope the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and prepare a short technical quickstart for your team.

Recap (from our call):
- Primary use case: real-time fraud scoring + classification (low single-digit 100ms goal per request).
- Models: 2-3 candidate open models (you asked about latency/cost tradeoffs).
- Initial plan: pilot on Hosted API to iterate quickly, then evaluate Dedicated/Private if we hit compliance or throughput needs.

What we need from you (quick asks):
1) Peak TPS / concurrency we should plan for (samples attached would help).
2) Typical prompt length and expected completion size (tokens).
3) Any data residency or compliance requirements (PCI, SOC2, HIPAA) that will push you away from Hosted initially.
4) Who on your infra/ops team should join the technical deep-dive?

Next steps on our side:
- I’ll put together a short Hosted quickstart checklist (API endpoints, sample curl, streaming guidance) and a suggested rate-limit profile for your pilot.
- Ben (cc) will scope capacity and provide rough Dedicated pricing if you want guaranteed throughput.
- If you send a traffic sample (jsonl) and a short SOW draft I can loop in Marissa (solutions engineer) and we’ll propose a 30-min technical call.

Attachments: traffic_samples.jsonl (placeholder), omnipay_sow_draft.pdf (if you have an internal SOW)

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

Best,

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the traffic sample you requested (traffic_samples.jsonl). High-level answers below: 

- Peak TPS: ~3 requests/sec (we expect bursts up to ~6 r/s for short windows during peak hours).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~30-40 simultaneous requests during peaks.
- Prompt size: median prompt ~20 tokens; median completion ~50 tokens. ~95th percentile completion ~400 tokens for a small subset.
- Latency requirement: end-to-end scoring goal <= 300ms 95th percentile; lower is better.
- Compliance: OmniPay is PCI-focused. For the pilot we can use Hosted API if tokens are redacted before we send queries; however, longer term we will need Private VPC/on-prem for full card-data flows. SOC2 is required; we also ask for data residency in us-east (or option to route to us-east).

Ops contact: Elena Cho (elena.cho@omnipay.ai) — she can join the technical call.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) What are the default per-client rate limits on Hosted (r/s and tokens/s)? How do you handle spikes?
2) Can we do prefix/KV caching to reduce token costs for repeated scoring?
3) Any recommended model variants for low-latency scoring at 1-3 r/s?

We can also share a short SOW draft (sending separately) if helpful. Thanks — happy to set up the tech call next week.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product, OmniPay
elena@omnipay.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & quickstart questions — Hosted API suitability

Elena — really helpful, thanks for the details and for looping in Elena Cho. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Answers to your questions:
- Default Hosted limits: 5 r/s per API key by default; soft token cap of 5000 tokens/min per key. These are conservative defaults for new signups; we can raise per-route caps for pilots.
- Handling spikes: we have per-key rate caps plus short-term burst allowances; if sustained throughput > your bursts we recommend either a Dedicated pool or an adjusted Hosted plan with explicit rate increases.
- Caching: yes — prefix/KV caching is supported in the runtime. For repeated scoring with identical prefixes we can cache KV state to eliminate duplicate model evals. That will materially reduce token usage.
- Model recommendations: for low latency scoring at modest throughput, try a trimmed-open LLM (quantized variant) — trade-off: slightly lower output richness but much faster per-token times. Marissa can propose specific variants during the tech call.

Hosted quickstart (short):
1) Create API key in Console -> API Keys.
2) Endpoint (text generation): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   - Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-lite","prompt":"<your prompt>","max_tokens":60}'
   - Streaming: add "stream": true to get server-sent events and lower perceived latency.
3) Rate-limit adjustments: open a support ticket / email sales-ops@redwood.com with sample traffic and requested caps; we can provision increased Hosted caps for pilots within 24–48 hours.
4) Observability: Console shows per-route token/latency breakdowns; we can add a trace hook for your infra team in the tech call.

Attachments: I’ve put a short quickstart doc in our Drive and attached a local copy (omnipay_quickstart_steps.md). I’ll also include a suggested initial rate-limit profile based on your numbers: burst to 10 r/s, steady 4 r/s, token cap 10k/min — this is a starting point we can iterate on.

Compliance note: Hosted is SOC2-compliant; PCI is tricky — for anything involving raw card data we recommend Private VPC or on-prem deployment. For the pilot you can tokenize/redact inputs and stay on Hosted if that meets your security team's rules. We can provide SOC2 report and data residency options (us-east) — I’ll attach the SOC2 onboarding packet in my next message.

Suggested next step: 30-minute technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) + Elena Cho to map endpoints, auth, and a short runbook for the pilot. Ben — can you propose availability?

Best,
Soojin
